newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Problems eased in Russian army, defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Problems eased in Russian army, defence minister.

text.p: Russian Defence Minster Igor Rodionov, who last week raised the alarm about the parlous state of the armed forces, said on Tuesday the situation had eased.
"I wouldn't call the situation in the Russian armed forces a crisis," Rodionov told reporters after meeting British Defence Minister Michael Portillo.

"There are certain complications and difficulties which we, especially the government, are overcoming. The situation a month ago was more difficult, but we have overcome it and today things are improving, including funding," he said.
A week ago Rodionov told a meeting of military top brass that Russia faced a catastrophe unless it took extreme measures to reform the army.
"The armed forces today have come to the point where a further reduction in their combat readiness could lead to unforeseeble, tragic consequences," Rodionov had said.
"If extreme measures are not taken to reform the army in the near future, the consequences for the state could be catastrophic."

Rodionov has played down talk of a military rebellion but said repeatedly that problems, which have included acute shortages in equipment and supplies and wage delays, could soon get out of control unless defence spending is increased.
